summary: First backend testing iteration after base44->FastAPI+MongoDB migration. All 22 backend tests PASS (100% success). Coverage: health endpoint, auth (register/login/me/duplicate/bad-password/no-token), MemoryNode full CRUD with persistence verification, seeded entity lists (Agent, Skill, AuditEvent, MonetaryProposal, FactionResonance), and all 7 function dispatchers (predictResonance, gemmaChat w/ Claude Opus 4.5, orchestrateAgent, indexDocument, retrieveContext, testSkill, checkPriceAlerts) plus unknown-function 404. Claude Opus 4.5 via emergentintegrations returns real (non-demo) content.

minor.issue: Logout is stateless (returns ok=true) with no token revocation/blacklist. Acceptable for JWT but documented as design choice, not a bug.
Telegram dispatch is stubbed (MOCKED as declared). No real notification sent; only last_alert_date is updated.
Embeddings are deterministic 128-dim hash-based pseudo-embeddings (MOCKED as declared). Cosine similarity works but retrieval quality is not semantic.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1018 lines — consider splitting into modules (auth.py, entities.py, functions/*.py, seed.py) for maintainability once features stabilize.

JWT_SECRET has a non-empty default in server.py line 36 ('aegis-q-sovereign-secret-change-me'). Although .env overrides it in practice, defaulting silently is risky; prefer failing fast if not set in production.

checkPriceAlerts: 'upper_threshold' trigger logic only fires once per call; no direction-change detection (e.g., crossed up vs crossed down). Acceptable for MVP but may cause alert spam/misses in real usage.

gemmaChat replays all prior user messages via chat.send_message before the final one (lines 326-329). With Claude Opus this is expensive (O(N) API calls per chat turn) and may hit rate limits / latency for long conversations. Consider using a single send with full history or a persistent session_id strategy.
entity_create/entity_update accept arbitrary Dict[str, Any] without per-entity pydantic validation — clients can store any shape. Consider per-entity schemas for at least Agent, Skill, MemoryNode.
predictResonance: population_std is computed as population stdev but used with a z>2 rule intended for sample stdev; for the 20-100 nodes involved the difference is negligible, but flag for review.
RAG embeddings (128-dim hash) are declared mocked but the code path is still named _generate_embedding — consider renaming to _pseudo_embedding to avoid confusion once real embeddings are wired.
seed_data_creation: Seeded on startup by server.py (22 MemoryNodes, 40 AuditEvents, 9 FactionResonance, 5 Agents, 5 Skills, 2 MonetaryProposals). Tests create & delete additional TEST_ prefixed data and one knowledge document that is left persisted.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use demo@aegis-q.mil / Aegis2026! to login. All 22 tests in /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py pass against https://hybrid-federated-ia.preview.emergentagent.com. Claude Opus calls take ~5-15s each; testSkill/orchestrateAgent/gemmaChat require timeouts >=60s. Emails with .test TLD are rejected by EmailStr validator — always use real-looking domains (aegis-q.mil, example.com, etc). If testing the frontend, focus on integration with the 50+ base44-mimicking pages via /app/frontend/src/api/base44Client.js drop-in.
